newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures firm again late, end stronger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures firm again late, end stronger.

text.p: U.S. debt futures firmed again into the close and finished with sizable gains but perched just below day's peaks.
December Treasury bond futures, after stalling on the upside and paring gains, managed to tick back up and touch the session's highest level and resistance at 109-10/32 minutes before the final bell.
But it again failed to overcome that barrier, which represented a 61.8 percent retracement of the contract's downmove to the Sept 6 low of 105-09/32 from its Aug 13 peak of 111-26/32.

"We died up at that top," said a T-bond futures floor broker, who said the ability of the contract to clear 109-10/32 likely would depend on the market's reaction to Thursday's five-year T-note auction.
Although some said Wednesday's two-year note sale was fairly well-received, they saw muted response in the long end.
"There was no reaction down here," said the T-bond broker.
"We didn't really react," agreed another T-bond broker, who called the afternoon's firming "a slow creep up."
The second broker, however, expected more gains near term, after a wave of big dealer buying early boosted the curve.

"I still think we're going higher," she said. "There was a lot of good dealer buying today across the curve. We could try to test the 110 handle. That 110-04/32 level has repeatedly been good support or resistance. Above there, I'd be really cautious about them."
December Euros stalled just below key resistance at 94.25, a level some said was more critical than the 94.28 double-top from mid-August, which they said was hit on scanty volume.
Some traders noted a change in outlook toward expecting no Fed rate hike before year end and cited massive customer buying in Euros from one dealer as fueling that sentiment.

Brokers estimated one firm covered as many as 40,000 total short contracts in the first four months of Eurodollars, while in the intermediate sector they had noted morning talk of central bank buying in two-, five- and 10-year T-notes.
"People went from one side of the boat to the other," said a Euro broker. "There's a shift in psychology, that we're not going to see much from the Fed before the end of the year."

December T-bonds added 19/32 to 109-07/32, T-notes gained 13/32 to 107-11/32, muni bonds added 10/32 to 113-30/32, T-bills rose five basis points to 94.79 and Eurodollars gained four basis points to 94.22. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
